doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

title: Teaching women students and demanding the bebop language
summary: She wants students fluent in jazz language, centered on Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Excellent. A couple of more questions, we’ve been at it for a while. Do you have female — women students at the university?
Glad to hear that. What — are there one or two things that you really demand that they absorb and are able to do or to know about before they graduate?

Yes. Again, that’s a really big question. I want them to be able to speak the language of jazz and that really means, to me, even though if they’re not into bebop but I want them to understand that language. And if they can’t really, I wish they could all really execute it and all really play it and be fluent in it, and that they are excited about it, but it’s at the core of whatever music or improvised music we’re going to end up playing but the language of Charlie Parker, to me, is just so central that I really do not let them off the hook. Even when they try, they pull out all the tricks you know, trying to distract me but I really try to get them excited about that. And most of the time I manage to — it doesn’t mean they end up being able to play like that but understanding how this language works.
